METALWORK — TERMLY EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: METALWORK
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.

2. When learning Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.

3. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Internal Cooking Timer
   B. Input Cable Tester
   C. International Cricket Team
   D. Information and Communication Technology

4. When learning Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.

5. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Remove all guards
   C. Work alone with eyes closed
   D. Wear safety gear and follow instructions

6. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

7. When learning Measuring and marking out tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Measuring and marking out tools.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Measuring and marking out tools.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring and marking out tools.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Measuring and marking out tools.

8. When learning Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)

   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.

9. When learning Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 , the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .
   C. Skip safety briefings for Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .

10. When learning Safety in the workshop, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Safety in the workshop.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Safety in the workshop.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety in the workshop.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Safety in the workshop.

11. When learning Hand tools and bench tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Hand tools and bench tools.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Hand tools and bench tools.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Hand tools and bench tools.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Hand tools and bench tools.

12. When learning Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.

13. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. CPU
   B. Keyboard
   C. Speaker
   D. Monitor

14. When learning Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro.

15. When learning Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.

16. When learning Introduction to Metalwork, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Metalwork.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Metalwork.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Metalwork.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Metalwork.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Metalwork and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
